newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms, trade still bullish for gas oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms, trade still bullish for gas oil.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures rose modestly early on Friday, but the November/December backwardation narrowed slightly taking some of the heat out of the market.
Brent crude futures rose, but traders expected the market to remain range-bound ahead of the weekend.
By 1105 GMT November gas oil was trading $1.25 a tonne higher at $222.00, while December gained $1.50 to $211.25.
"The spread has narrowed a little, but it is still looking steady," said one broker.
The broker said there was a good chance gas oil could extend the rally during the run-up to the November expiry on Tuesday.
"Gas oil has got a life of its own," he said. "Talk of a squeeze has put the fear of God into everyone because it makes it easy to push the market higher," he added.

"With colder weather in Europe and the first significant frost of the winter seen in the UK last night, there is likely to be further buying of nearby futures ahead of the weekend," said brokers GNI in their daily energy report.
And values would not necessarily retrace significantly after the expiry, traders and brokers said.
"It is the wrong time of the year to go and restructure yourself short," the broker said.
"There is always the chance of another squeeze next month as well."
December Brent was 17 cents a barrel up at $22.38.
Some traders said the market looked range-bound short term, although the risk of further tests of support remained.

"The market will probably hold a $22.10 to $22.50 range today," said a broker. "Another test of support at $22.10 today is by no means out of the question unless the bulls step back into products again," GNI said.
Traders said the International Energy Agency's (IEA) monthly oil market report had little bearing on prices.
While world oil demand was projected to rise this winter, the IEA also said the stock shortfall would be alleviated during the fourth quarter of 1996, brokers said.
